## Project Overview

This notebook prepares **CYBHI EBP/CDEP** satisfaction survey data for analysis and reporting. It ingests four raw exports from the eInsight clinical management platform (one per respondent type), processes the two-row hierarchical headers, removes test/demo accounts, and writes one cleaned CSV per survey type plus a combined file for use by downstream analysis scripts.

**Data sources (eInsight exports):**

- **Satisfaction Survey — Caregiver** — Respondents who are caregivers of a child receiving services.
- **Satisfaction Survey — Child (13–17)** — Respondents who are youth ages 13–17.
- **Satisfaction Survey — Adult (18–59)** — Respondents who are adults ages 18–59.
- **Satisfaction Survey — Adult (60+)** — Respondents who are older adults age 60 and above.

Each file has a two-row header: row 1 contains question text (with merged cells exported as `NA`), and row 2 contains subheader labels (e.g., "Rating", "Comments"). These are combined into clean column names using `zoo::na.locf()` to forward-fill the question text across merged cells.

**Demo filter:** rows whose `provider_id` contains "DEMO" are removed. Rows with a missing `provider_id` are **kept** and counted (previously they were dropped as a side effect of the filter). Unlike the assessment scripts, rows with no `client_system_id` are also kept, because a survey response without a client ID is still a valid response.

**Data window (D1):** survey responses dated from `start_date` (2024-01-01) through `end_date` (2027-03-31) go into the combined file.

**Outputs:**

| File | Contents |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `satisfaction_caregiver_clean.csv` | Cleaned caregiver survey responses (demo rows removed; no date cleaning or period filter) |
| `satisfaction_child_clean.csv` | Cleaned child (13–17) survey responses |
| `satisfaction_adult_clean.csv` | Cleaned adult (18–59) survey responses |
| `satisfaction_senior_clean.csv` | Cleaned adult (60+) survey responses |
| `combined_satisfaction_clean.csv` | All four surveys combined, with cleaned dates, period filter, `year`, and `quarter_label` — **primary input for downstream analysis** |

# Helper Functions

The header-processing logic is identical across all four survey files (and the assessment cleaning scripts).

```{r helpers}
# ---- Shared helpers (identical across the cleaning scripts) ----

# Reads an eInsight assessment CSV export with two-row headers.
# Row 1 holds question text (merged cells export as blanks and are forward-
# filled); row 2 holds sub-headers ("Response", "Score", ...). Returns a data
# frame with combined snake_case names and fully blank columns removed.
# "0" is deliberately NOT treated as missing: it is a valid rating on most tools.
read_assessment_csv <- function(path, na_vals = c("-", "", "NA", "N/A")) {
  raw <- read_csv(path, na = na_vals, col_names = FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE,
                  col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

  h1    <- unlist(raw[1, ], use.names = FALSE)
  h2    <- unlist(raw[2, ], use.names = FALSE)
  h1_ff <- na.locf(h1, na.rm = FALSE) |> str_squish()

  new_names <- ifelse(
    is.na(h1_ff) | h1_ff == "",
    h2,
    paste(h1_ff, h2, sep = " - ")
  )
  new_names <- janitor::make_clean_names(new_names)

  df <- raw[-c(1, 2), ]
  names(df) <- new_names

  df |> select(where(~ !all(is.na(.))))
}

# Parses eInsight date strings in ISO (2024-03-15) or US (03/15/2024) format,
# with or without a time stamp. Warns with a count of non-blank values that
# could not be parsed (these become NA and are dropped by the date filter).
parse_einsight_date <- function(x, label = "date_completed") {
  x   <- na_if(str_squish(as.character(x)), "")
  out <- as.Date(parse_date_time(
    x,
    orders = c("Ymd", "mdY", "mdy", "Ymd HMS", "Ymd HM", "mdY HMS", "mdY HM"),
    quiet  = TRUE
  ))
  n_bad <- sum(!is.na(x) & is.na(out))
  if (n_bad > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_bad, " non-blank value(s) could not be parsed as dates and were set to NA.",
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  out
}

# Reads a satisfaction survey CSV and removes rows whose provider_id contains
# "DEMO". Rows with a missing provider_id are kept (and counted).
read_satisfaction_survey <- function(path, label) {
  df <- read_assessment_csv(path)

  is_demo <- coalesce(str_detect(as.character(df$provider_id), "DEMO"), FALSE)
  cat(label, "- rows read:", nrow(df),
      "| DEMO rows removed:", sum(is_demo),
      "| rows with missing provider_id (kept):", sum(is.na(df$provider_id)), "\n")

  df[!is_demo, ]
}
```

# 1. Read and Clean Survey Files

## 1.1 Caregiver

```{r read-caregiver}
caregiver <- read_satisfaction_survey(file.path(in_dir, "Satisfaction_survey-caregiver.csv"), "Caregiver")
```

## 1.2 Child (13–17)

```{r read-child}
child <- read_satisfaction_survey(file.path(in_dir, "Satisfaction_survey-child_13-17.csv"), "Child")
```

## 1.3 Adult (18–59)

```{r read-adult}
adult <- read_satisfaction_survey(file.path(in_dir, "Satisfaction_survey-adult_18-59.csv"), "Adult")
```

## 1.4 Adult (60+)

```{r read-senior}
senior <- read_satisfaction_survey(file.path(in_dir, "Satisfaction_survey-adult_60_plus.csv"), "Senior")
```

# 2. Quick Checks

Row counts, a check that no DEMO records remain after filtering, and a list of provider IDs that look like test accounts but were not caught by the "DEMO" rule (review these; they are not removed).

```{r checks}
surveys <- list(caregiver = caregiver, child = child, adult = adult, senior = senior)

purrr::imap_dfr(surveys, ~ {
  tibble(
    survey                = .y,
    n_rows                = nrow(.x),
    n_demo_remaining      = sum(str_detect(as.character(.x$provider_id), "DEMO"), na.rm = TRUE),
    n_missing_provider_id = sum(is.na(.x$provider_id)),
    n_missing_client_id   = sum(is.na(.x$client_system_id))
  )
})

# Possible test accounts not caught by the "DEMO" rule
purrr::imap_dfr(surveys, ~ .x |>
  filter(str_detect(as.character(provider_id), regex("demo|test", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  count(provider_id, name = "n_rows") |>
  mutate(survey = .y, .before = 1))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 3. Create Combined Dataset

Bind all four survey types into a single data frame, clean malformed dates, filter to the reporting period, and add `quarter_label` and `year` columns. The `source` column identifies which survey each row came from.

**Date cleaning rationale:** Some date_completed values have year prefixes of `00` or `29` (e.g., "0024-03-15" or "2924-03-15"), likely from data entry errors in eInsight. These are corrected to `20` before converting to Date.

**Period filter:** Rows with no valid date, with `date_clean` before `start_date`, or after `end_date` are excluded. The counts for each reason are printed below.

```{r create-combined}
combined_raw <- bind_rows(
  caregiver |> mutate(source = "caregiver"),
  child     |> mutate(source = "child"),
  adult     |> mutate(source = "adult"),
  senior    |> mutate(source = "senior")
) |>
  mutate(
    date_clean = str_replace(date_completed, "^00", "20"),
    date_clean = str_replace(date_clean,     "^29", "20"),
    date_clean = parse_einsight_date(date_clean, label = "Satisfaction date_completed")
  )

cat("Rows before period filter:   ", nrow(combined_raw), "\n")
cat("  Year prefix corrected:     ", sum(str_detect(combined_raw$date_completed, "^(00|29)"), na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("  Dropped - no valid date:   ", sum(is.na(combined_raw$date_clean)), "\n")
cat("  Dropped - before start:    ", sum(combined_raw$date_clean < start_date, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("  Dropped - after end:       ", sum(combined_raw$date_clean > end_date, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

combined_all <- combined_raw |>
  filter(between(date_clean, start_date, end_date)) |>
  mutate(
    year          = year(date_clean),
    quarter_label = paste0("Q", quarter(date_clean), " ", year(date_clean))
  ) |>
  # Sort chronologically so quarter_label order is preserved when read back from CSV
  arrange(date_clean)

cat("Combined rows:", nrow(combined_all), "\n")
cat("Date range:   ", format(min(combined_all$date_clean)), "to",
                      format(max(combined_all$date_clean)), "\n")

combined_all |> count(source)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 4. Write Clean CSVs

Individual survey files are written for reference. The combined file is the primary input for downstream analysis.

```{r write-csvs}
write_csv(caregiver,    file.path(out_dir, "satisfaction_caregiver_clean.csv"))
write_csv(child,        file.path(out_dir, "satisfaction_child_clean.csv"))
write_csv(adult,        file.path(out_dir, "satisfaction_adult_clean.csv"))
write_csv(senior,       file.path(out_dir, "satisfaction_senior_clean.csv"))
write_csv(combined_all, file.path(out_dir, "combined_satisfaction_clean.csv"))

cat("CSVs written successfully.\n")
```
